name: Fair Isaac (FICO)
description: FICO owns the FICO Score, the standard measure of consumer credit risk used in most U.S. credit decisions by banks, card issuers, mortgage lenders and auto lenders. It earns a royalty each time a score is used, mostly paid through the three major credit bureaus (Experian, TransUnion and Equifax), and it also sells scores directly to consumers (myFICO). Its second segment sells decision-management and analytics software (fraud detection, account origination, customer management) as SaaS or on-premises licences. Scores drove 59 percent of FY2025 revenue and 81 percent of segment operating income; a higher per-score price on mortgage originations was the main reason B2B scores revenue rose. The FHFA, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac decide which credit scores can be used on mortgages they buy, which is the main regulatory exposure named in the 10-K.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 7389 (Services-Business Services). The box hides that the larger, far more profitable half is not software: in FY2025 the Scores segment earned about 88 percent margins and 81 percent of segment operating income by licensing the FICO Score, a per-use royalty on U.S. credit decisions distributed mostly through Experian, TransUnion and Equifax, with the bureaus alone at 51 percent of total revenue.

hq.note: 5 West Mendenhall, Suite 105, Bozeman, MT (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in Delaware

employees.note: Employees at fiscal year-end, up 6% from 3,586 (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Scores
businessLines.how: A per-use royalty: lenders and other users pay each time a FICO Score is pulled or used in a credit decision (mostly via the bureaus, which pay FICO under agreements), with volume tied to U.S. credit applications and mortgage originations and the unit price FICO sets, plus a multi-year licence on its insurance score and small consumer subscriptions.
businessLines.description: Business-to-business (B2B) scoring (FICO Score and other scores, distributed mainly through the credit bureaus and, for some products, sold directly) and business-to-consumer (B2C) scores (myFICO.com subscriptions and royalties on scores sold indirectly to consumers through the bureaus).

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating income, before unallocated corporate costs; FY2024 $813.4M; FY2023 $681.1M

businessLines.name: Software
businessLines.how: Annual or multi-year subscription and licence fees from banks and other large enterprises for software they run on their own decisions, with recurring revenue tracked as Annual Recurring Revenue, plus one-off professional-services fees for implementation.
businessLines.description: Pre-configured analytic and decision-management solutions for account origination, customer management, customer engagement, fraud detection and marketing, plus professional services, and the FICO Platform, a modular decisioning offering; delivered as SaaS or on-premises.

revenue.note: +3% vs $797.9M FY2024; $739.7M FY2023. On-premises and SaaS software $740.1M and professional services $82.1M. 9 months FY2026 about $639.4M (software $584.4M + services $55.0M) vs about $618.1M; Q3 FY2026 $215.3M vs $212.1M (+2%)
